route: Free search: the run-level Holt-Klee obstruction for one-player all-switches, and walk realisation as a linear programme in the value vectors (labels fs15:)
headline: A one-player all-switches RUN (not just the orientation) is the bottom-antipodal walk of a Holt-Klee AUSO unless the game is tied at two incidences of the run whose occupancy differences positively span 0. Consequences, all unconditional and degenerate-case included: f_1(4)=6 < 7 = f(4) (the first separation of one-player from two-player all-switches at fixed m); the walk of the SECOND BLOW-UP LEVEL B^2 is not realisable by any one-player game; nor is the walk of the h*(5)=12 witness of prop:hstar-five. The escape hypothesis is not vacuous -- an explicit 31-vertex one-player game exhibits it. Seed (A) is answered: TOP is target-equivalent.
gap: Whether a one-player stopping SSG can have an all-switches run of length exceeding h*_HK(m): equivalently, whether the configuration of fs15:two-ties-cor(i) -- two tied incidences (t_1,v),(t_2,v) at one Max vertex with sigma_{t_1}(v) != sigma_{t_2}(v), whose occupancy differences y^{sigma_{t_1}} - y^{sigma_{t_1}[v]} and y^{sigma_{t_2}} - y^{sigma_{t_2}[v]} are anti-parallel -- can occur on a run longer than h*_HK(m).
next_steps: (1) The cheapest decisive next computation is f_1(5): run fs15:screen (the completion + tie test, /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/free-search-15/t_b2_ties.py, ~0-4 s per walk) on every length-12 bottom-antipodal sequence of the 5-cube. prop:hstar-five's own enumeration counts 347640 from sigma_0=0, about 2900 up to the 120 coordinate permutations fixing sigma_0; the sequence enumeration itself needs the C program census/hstar.c (about 70 million nodes, seconds in C, hours in Python). A clean f_1(5) <= 11 would extend the separation and would say that no one-player game attains h*(5).  (2) Close or exploit the gap: either prove that fs15:two-ties-cor(i) forces L <= h*_HK(m) (the extra necessary conditions it already yields -- switching v leaves the expected occupancy of every disagreeing coordinate exactly unchanged -- look strong enough to push further), or engineer an instance realising it on a long run, which would be the first one-player family to escape the Holt-Klee ceiling.  (3) Since the one-player half of the pivot is now, modulo that gap, the purely combinatorial question whether h*_HK(m) is superpolynomial, measure h*_HK(6) or find an HK-preserving height amplifier; the paper's blowhk.py only searched one rule family, and lem:hstar-super's twisted product has not been tested for Holt-Klee preservation (a five-minute computation that would give h*_HK superadditive, hence >= 2.2m).  (4) The two-player half is untouched by all this and is where B^2 must now be realised; fs_two.py gives an exact decoupled LP for it once the value vectors and Min responses are guessed, but a better outer search than mine is needed (mine fails on the calibration target).

results.name: fs15:tie-partner
results.statement: Let G be stopping with |Vmax|=m, let sigma_0..sigma_L be its all-switches run with switched sets S_t, and let s' be the AUSO of cor:ceiling-general (s'(sigma_t)=S_t). If the incidence (sigma_t,v) is tied then (a) v not in S_t and val_{sigma_t[v]} = val_{sigma_t}; (b) S(sigma_t[v]) = S_t; (c) sigma_t[v] is NOT on the run; (d) s'(sigma_t[v]) = S_t u {v}.
results.argument: (a) is lem:trichotomy. (b) the margin at u != v depends only on the value vector and on sigma(u), both unchanged; at v both incidences are tied. (c) the strategies of a run lie in pairwise distinct flat classes (lem:flat-class(c)), i.e. carry distinct value vectors, while a tie makes val_{sigma_t[v]} = val_{sigma_t}. (d) lem:flat-class makes the flat class a subcube on which S and the flat direction set D are constant with v in D; cor:ceiling-general's resolution takes the class corner to be sigma_t, so thm:flat-resolution's formula gives S_t u {v}.
results.verification: Purely deductive from lem:trichotomy, lem:flat-class, thm:flat-resolution, cor:ceiling-general. Its combinatorial content (the 'legal candidate tie' predicate) is what the exhaustive enumerations in t_ties7full.py, t_b2_ties.py, t_h12.py compute.

results.name: fs15:run-hk
results.statement: Let G be stopping with Vmin empty, |Vmax|=m, all-switches run sigma_0..sigma_L. Let T be the set of tied incidences (t,v) on the run and D_{t,v} := y^{sigma_t} - y^{sigma_t[v]} in R^{2m}, the difference of two vertices of the occupancy polytope X(G) of prop:oneplayer-lp. If 0 is not in conv{D_{t,v} : (t,v) in T} -- vacuous when T is empty, automatic when |T| <= 1, and whenever the D_{t,v} are linearly independent -- then there is a HOLT-KLEE AUSO of the m-cube whose bottom-antipodal walk from sigma_0 is exactly the run. In particular L <= h*_HK(m).
results.argument: X(G) depends only on the transition part of the harmonic normal form, so perturbing the objective (= perturbing the payoffs q) moves no vertex. By thm:impedance summed over w, obj(y^{sigma[v]}) - obj(y^sigma) is a POSITIVE multiple of the incidence margin, an identity needing no nondegeneracy. Each D_{t,v} is nonzero (different supports), so by the separating hyperplane theorem the hypothesis gives c with <c,D_{t,v}> > 0 on T; the c that are constant on some edge form a finite union of hyperplanes, so c can be chosen generic as well. For small eps > 0, obj + eps c is generic on X(G), hence an LP orientation of a simple polytope combinatorially equivalent to the m-cube, hence an AUSO satisfying Holt-Klee (Holt-Klee; Gaertner-Morris-Ruest). At the run's strategies the untied incidences keep their sign and the tied ones are oriented INTO sigma_t, so the outmap there is exactly S_t and the bottom-antipodal walk from sigma_0 is the run.
results.verification: Deductive, from prop:oneplayer-lp and thm:impedance as printed in frontier.tex. Its two numerical inputs were re-verified independently: h*(4)=7 with a unique class and h*_HK(4)=6 recomputed from the census of all 12640 AUSO classes of the 4-cube (t_hk4.py), and cross-checked with an INDEPENDENT Holt-Klee test (exhaustive vertex-disjoint monotone path packing, no max-flow, fs_hk.py/t_hk_cross.py): 0 disagreements on all 12640 classes.

results.name: fs15:two-ties + fs15:two-ties-cor
results.statement: If (t_1,v_1),(t_2,v_2) are tied incidences on the run of a one-player stopping SSG with v_1 != v_2 and sigma_{t_2}(v_1) != sigma_{t_1}(v_1), then 0 is not in conv{D_{t_1,v_1}, D_{t_2,v_2}}. Hence a two-element tie set escapes fs15:run-hk only if (i) the two ties sit at the SAME Max vertex with opposite actions, or (ii) at different vertices at which the two run strategies agree. In case (i) the two strategies must differ at some u != v, and at every such u switching v leaves the expected total occupancy of u exactly unchanged.
results.argument: Read the coordinate (v_1, a) with a = sigma_{t_1}(v_1). y^sigma is supported on {(u,sigma(u))} with entries >= 1, so D_{t_1,v_1} has entry >= 1 there while sigma_{t_2} and sigma_{t_2}[v_2] both take action 1-a at v_1 (they differ only at v_2), so D_{t_2,v_2} vanishes there. A convex combination summing to 0 forces c_1 = 0, hence D_{t_2,v_2} = 0, false. For the corollary: same-vertex ties with the SAME action give two positive entries at (v,a), forcing both coefficients to 0; and in case (i) sigma_{t_2} is neither sigma_{t_1} nor sigma_{t_1}[v] (the latter is off the run by fs15:tie-partner(c)), so they differ off v, and reading the coordinate (u, sigma_{t_1}(u)) at each such u kills the corresponding entry of D_{t_1,v}.
results.verification: Deductive. The dichotomy is confirmed empirically: all three escapes found by random sampling (t_escape.py, m=3 den 4 and 8, m=4 den 8) are of type (i), same vertex, opposite actions.

results.name: fs15:f1-four
results.statement: No stopping SSG with Vmin empty and |Vmax| = 4 has an all-switches run of length 7, degenerate or not; and one with a run of length 6 exists. So f_1(4) = 6 < 7 = f(4) = h*(4).
results.argument: A run of length 7 makes cor:ceiling-general's AUSO have height exactly 7 = h*(4), hence lie in the unique height-7 class (384 outmaps). Over that whole orbit and all 768 length-7 bottom-antipodal walks, the incidences a tie could occupy by fs15:tie-partner(c),(d) -- v not in S_t, s'(sigma_t xor 2^v) = S_t | 2^v, partner off the walk -- number at most ONE. So |T| <= 1, fs15:run-hk gives a Holt-Klee AUSO of the 4-cube with a length-7 walk, and h*_HK(4) = 6. For the lower bound, the paper's one-player game AP_m4_k0_den256_s200 is stopping, nondegenerate, and its run from sigma = 2 is 2,8,5,9,13,14,15.
results.verification: t_ties7.py, t_ties7full.py (orbit of 384 outmaps built by hand from the height-7 representative, 768 walks examined; every walk has exactly one candidate whose partner is ON the walk, which a tie forbids, and at most one legal one). t_hk4.py and the independent t_hk_cross.py for h*(4)=7 unique and h*_HK(4)=6. t_f1_four.py recomputes the length-6 run, the outmap, stopping and nondegeneracy of AP_m4_k0_den256_s200 in exact rational arithmetic from its normal form. All re-run with assertions in t_verify_all.py (verify_all.log: ALL CHECKS PASSED).

results.name: fs15:b2-oneplayer
results.statement: No stopping SSG with Vmin empty has the bottom-antipodal walk 13,18,12,16,9,17,1,6,0,4,5 of the SECOND BLOW-UP LEVEL B^2 (5-cube, height 10) as its all-switches run -- degenerate or not. So the second level of thm:blowup needs Min vertices for its WALK, not only for its orientation, and not only in the nondegenerate case.
results.argument: Exhaustive depth-first enumeration of all outmaps of the 5-cube agreeing with the walk's eleven values and satisfying Szabo-Welzl (which forces injectivity) gives 1897 USOs, 875 acyclic (B^2 among them), and NONE Holt-Klee. So by fs15:run-hk the tie set is non-separable, whence |T| >= 2; and over all 875 the legal candidate tie sets are only {}, {(7,3)}, {(5,2)} and {(5,2),(7,3)}. Hence T = {(5,2),(7,3)}. Now sigma_5 = 17 has action 0 at Max vertex x_2 while sigma_7 = 6 and sigma_7[x_3] = 14 both have action 1 there, so fs15:two-ties applies and contradicts non-separability.
results.verification: fs_blow.py rebuilds thm:blowup's B from scratch and t_b2.py checks B(1-cube) (AUSO, height 4, Holt-Klee) and B^2 (USO, acyclic, height 10, NOT Holt-Klee) with this route's own predicates; the first level comes out as the paper's orientation translated by 1, so the orbit is the paper's. t_b2_ties.py does the enumeration (4 s) and t_verify_all.py repeats it with assertions, including the check that B^2 itself is among the 875 completions and that every legal candidate set is a subset of {(5,2),(7,3)}. Holt-Klee via my_D.is_holt_klee, cross-validated against the independent fs_hk.hk on all 12640 4-cube classes.

results.name: fs15:h12-oneplayer
results.statement: No stopping SSG with Vmin empty has 0,15,24,31,20,23,18,14,26,10,2,3,1 -- the length-12 = h*(5) bottom-antipodal walk of the outmap printed in prop:hstar-five -- as its all-switches run.
results.argument: The thirteen prescribed outmap values determine the orientation uniquely: the completion enumeration returns exactly one outmap, the printed one, and it is not Holt-Klee. So fs15:run-hk forces |T| >= 2, while fs15:tie-partner(c),(d) leaves only the two candidates (t,v) = (0,4) and (7,1), with partners 16 and 12 off the run. Hence T is both of them; but sigma_7 = 14 has action 1 at x_1 and sigma_0 = 0 has action 0 there, so fs15:two-ties applies.
results.verification: t_h12.py: one USO completion, acyclic, Holt-Klee false, candidate tie set exactly {(0,4),(7,1)}; runs in under a second.

results.name: fs15:escape-real
results.statement: The separability hypothesis of fs15:run-hk is NOT vacuous. There is a one-player stopping SSG with four Max vertices, harmonic normal form of denominator 8, whose all-switches run 6,0,10 carries two tied incidences at the SAME Max vertex x_3 with opposite actions, and whose occupancy differences satisfy D_{2,x_3} = -(880/819) D_{0,x_3}, so 0 lies in their convex hull.
results.argument: This refutes the hope that fs15:run-hk holds unconditionally by the argument given (i.e. that the tie set is always separable); the rows are printed in fs15:escape-real. It does NOT refute the conclusion L <= h*_HK(m): this instance's run has length 2, well under h*_HK(4) = 6.
results.verification: t_escape2.py reproduces the instance from the normal form in exact rational arithmetic (value vectors, all sixteen margins, both occupancy vertices, the exact ratio 880/819). t_escape_game.py then builds an EXPLICIT stopping SSG on 31 vertices (4 Max, 25 average, 2 sinks) by the Knuth-Yao gadget and recomputes the run, the value vectors and the two ties from the game with mycore's profile_value and trap-based is_stopping -- a fully independent code path; all agree. Frequency: over 15000 games at m=3 den 8 (120000 runs, 38782 carrying a tie) exactly one escape; over 4000 games at m=4 den 8 (64000 runs, 24090 with a tie) exactly one. All escapes found are of type fs15:two-ties-cor(i).

results.name: fs15:walk-lp
results.statement: Fix a walk sigma_0..sigma_L, value vectors x_0..x_L in R^{m+k} and Min actions tau_0..tau_L. Then the conditions saying that a harmonic normal form is stopping, has value vectors x_t at the sigma_t, and has all-switches run exactly sigma_0..sigma_L, are LINEAR in the 2(m+k) rows, and the conditions for distinct rows involve disjoint unknowns: the problem splits into 2(m+k) independent linear programmes in m+k+1 nonnegative unknowns and at most L+2 constraints. Ties off the run are unconstrained; ties on it are the inequalities met with equality.
results.argument: Strict substochasticity makes each frozen operator a contraction, so the equalities plus the Min inequalities say exactly that x_t is val_{sigma_t}, and the Max inequalities say exactly that S(sigma_t) = S_t. Only the L+1 strategies of the run are constrained, because the run visits only those. Disjointness is immediate: the row (w,a) occurs in no condition indexed by another (w',a'). This inverts the parametrisation used by prop:auso-seven's and rem:blowup-measured's searches (rows unknown, values a rational function of them, every condition nonlinear).
results.verification: t_validate.py: from the five value vectors of the paper's first-level realisation G_m3_k0_den64_s1 alone, the exact LPs return a stopping game whose run from sigma=4 is again 4,3,5,1,0. t_gsharp.py: G# is rebuilt from the paper's printed normal form (its outmap reproduced exactly, an independent check of prop:auso-seven), and from its eight value vectors and Min responses alone the exact two-player LPs return a stopping game whose run from sigma=8 is again 8,6,11,7,13,5,1,0.

results.name: fs15:nu-half (seed A, first half)
results.statement: For stopping G with Vavg nonempty and nu := max over Vavg of val, every value is 1 or at most nu, and nu lies in {0} u [1/2,1]; dually the least positive letter is at most 1/2, and the letters 1 = lambda_1 > lambda_2 > ... satisfy lambda_i >= 2^{1-i}. Consequently 'does SOME vertex have value at least 1/2?' is decided in linear time by the free attractor sweeps, while 'does THIS vertex?' is the target.
results.argument: All of it is one line from lem:alphabet-cover, which the paper already has: every letter in (0,1) is attained at an average vertex and is the mean of a strictly larger and a strictly smaller letter. The only letter above nu is 1, so nu = (1+lambda)/2 >= 1/2; and lambda_i >= lambda_{i-1}/2 gives the geometric bound. The seed's requested first step is therefore already in frontier.tex and should be cited, not reproved.

results.name: fs15:top (seed A)
results.statement: TOP -- given a stopping SSG with Vavg nonempty, output an average vertex of maximum value -- is polynomial-time equivalent to SSG-Value, by a reduction making a SINGLE oracle call. THIS ROUTE THEREFORE ENDS AT A TARGET-EQUIVALENT STATEMENT for seed (A), and says so.
results.argument: Reduce the comparison of two vertices (target-equivalent by prop:no-halving(b)). Collapse the value-1 and value-0 sets with the free attractor sweeps so that every non-sink value is in (0,1); let a = |Vavg|, r = 2a+2, m = r+2. Adjoin a reference chain e_1 -> (t1,t0), e_{j+1} -> (t1,e_j) of r average vertices (values 1-2^{-j}) and two boost chains c_p^{(1)} -> (t1,p), c_q^{(1)} -> (e_r,q), each continued by c^{(j+1)} -> (t1,c^{(j)}) for m steps. Then val(c_p^{(m)}) = 1-(1-val p)/2^m and val(c_q^{(m)}) = 1-(1-val q+2^{-r})/2^m, both at least 1-2^{-(r+1)}, which exceeds every old average value (<= 1-2^{-a} by lem:denominator-sharp) and every val(e_j) <= 1-2^{-r}; within each chain the values increase, so the maximum is at c_p^{(m)} or c_q^{(m)}, and it is at c_p^{(m)} exactly when val(p) > val(q) - 2^{-r}, which by lem:denominator-sharp (distinct values differ by at least 2^{-2a} > 2^{-r}) holds exactly when val(p) >= val(q). The maximiser is unique and O(a) vertices are added.
results.verification: t_top.py builds the reduction and checks it against brute-force wstar on random stopping games (random DAGs plus back edges kept only when still stopping), exact rational arithmetic: 4114 applicable instances over two seeds, 0 wrong, and in every case the argmax over Vavg was unique and was the predicted chain top.

results.name: searches for a two-player realisation of the B^2 walk
results.statement: Searches using fs15:walk-lp for a game realising the B^2 walk with one and with two Min vertices did not converge; nor did the calibration search for G#'s own walk, which IS realisable.
results.argument: Two outer searches were used: over the value vectors directly (fs_es3.py) and over the game manifold with the LP as an inner optimal repair (fs_es4.py, which keeps the equality half exactly satisfied so the score is the pure sign-violation optimum). Four seeds on G# (m=4,k=2) and two seeds each on B^2 with k=1 and k=2, 20-25 minutes each. All plateau at a total hinge violation of 5.6e-3 to 9.1e-3 after 3-6 x 10^4 evaluations.
results.verification: g4_k2_*.log, b4_k1_*.log, b4_k2_*.log in the code directory. Because the calibration target fails as well, these runs are evidence about the search, NOT about the instances -- exactly the caveat rem:blowup-measured records for the earlier searches. Reported here only so that nobody re-spends the budget on the same tool.

\subsection{One-player all-switches runs are Holt--Klee walks}\label{sec:fs15}

\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} bounds the improvement \emph{orientation} of a
\emph{nondegenerate} one-player game, and \Cref{rem:oneplayer-lp} records that
the hypothesis is genuine: the longest one-player runs in this document are
degenerate, and \Cref{thm:flat-resolution} resolves those into orientations
that need not be Holt--Klee. This subsection removes the hypothesis at the only
place where it matters, namely along the run itself, and draws two conclusions:
the one-player and two-player run lengths already separate at $m=4$, and the
second level of \Cref{thm:blowup} needs Min vertices for its \emph{walk} and
not merely for its orientation.

\begin{definition}[One-player run length; the Holt--Klee ceiling]\label{fs15:def-f1}
Let $f_1(m)$ be the greatest length of an all-switches run of a stopping SSG
with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $|\Vmax|=m$, and let $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$ be
the greatest bottom-antipodal height of a Holt--Klee AUSO of the $m$-cube. By
\Cref{cor:ceiling-general}, $f_1(m)\le h^{\ast}(m)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Where a tie on a run can sit]\label{fs15:tie-partner}
Let $G$ be stopping with $|\Vmax|=m$, let $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ be an
all-switches run with switched sets $S_t$, and let $s'$ be the AUSO supplied by
\Cref{cor:ceiling-general}, so $s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ for every $t$. Suppose the
incidence $(\sigma_t,v)$ is tied, i.e.\
$\val_{\sigma_t}(\bar\sigma_t(v))=\val_{\sigma_t}(\sigma_t(v))$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $v\notin S_t$ and $\val_{\sigma_t[v]}=\val_{\sigma_t}$;
\item $S(\sigma_t[v])=S_t$;
\item $\sigma_t[v]\notin\{\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L\}$;
\item $s'(\sigma_t[v])=S_t\cup\{v\}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) A tie is not a strict improvement, so $v\notin S_t$; the equality of the
value vectors is \Cref{lem:trichotomy}. (b) For $u\ne v$ the margin
$\val_{\sigma}(\bar\sigma(u))-\val_\sigma(\sigma(u))$ depends only on the value
vector and on $\sigma(u)$, and $\sigma_t[v]$ agrees with $\sigma_t$ at $u$ and
carries the same value vector by (a); at $v$ both incidences are tied. (c) By
\Cref{lem:flat-class}(c) the strategies of a run lie in pairwise distinct flat
classes, that is, they carry pairwise distinct value vectors, while
$\val_{\sigma_t[v]}=\val_{\sigma_t}$. (d) By \Cref{lem:flat-class} the flat
class $A$ of $\sigma_t$ is a subcube on which $S$ and the flat direction set
$D$ are constant, and $v\in D$; the resolution of
\Cref{cor:ceiling-general} takes $c_A:=\sigma_t$, so by
\Cref{thm:flat-resolution}
$s'(\sigma_t[v])=S(\sigma_t[v])\cup\{i\in D:\sigma_t[v]_i\ne(\sigma_t)_i\}
 =S_t\cup\{v\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A one-player run is the walk of a Holt--Klee AUSO]\label{fs15:run-hk}
Let $G$ be a stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $|\Vmax|=m$, let
$\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ be its all-switches run, let
\[
  T:=\{(t,v)\ :\ 0\le t\le L,\ (\sigma_t,v)\ \text{is a tied incidence}\},
  \qquad
  D_{t,v}:=y^{\sigma_t}-y^{\sigma_t[v]}\in\mathbb R^{2m},
\]
with $y^{\sigma}$ the vertices of the occupancy polytope $X(G)$ of
\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}. If
\[
  0\ \notin\ \operatorname{conv}\{D_{t,v}:(t,v)\in T\}
\]
--- vacuously when $T=\emptyset$, automatically when $|T|\le1$, and more
generally whenever the $D_{t,v}$ are linearly independent --- then there is a
Holt--Klee AUSO of the $m$-cube whose bottom-antipodal walk from $\sigma_0$ is
exactly $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$. In particular
$L\le h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$X(G)$ depends only on the transition part of the normal form, not on the
payoff part, and by \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} it is a simple $m$-polytope whose
vertices are the $y^{\sigma}$, whose graph is the $m$-cube and whose faces are
its subcubes; that argument uses only that $G$ is stopping. Its objective
$\mathrm{obj}$ satisfies
$\mathrm{obj}(y^{\sigma[v]})-\mathrm{obj}(y^{\sigma})
 =\kappa_{\sigma,v}\bigl(\val_\sigma(\bar\sigma(v))-\val_\sigma(\sigma(v))\bigr)$
with $\kappa_{\sigma,v}=\sum_w h(w\!\to\!v)/(1-h(b\!\to\!v))>0$, by
\Cref{thm:impedance} summed over $w$; this identity needs no nondegeneracy.

Each $D_{t,v}$ is nonzero, since $y^{\sigma_t}$ and $y^{\sigma_t[v]}$ have
different supports. By hypothesis and the separating hyperplane theorem there
is $c\in\mathbb R^{2m}$ with $\langle c,D_{t,v}\rangle>0$ for every
$(t,v)\in T$. The set of such $c$ is a nonempty open cone, and the $c$ that are
constant on some edge of $X(G)$ form a finite union of hyperplanes, so $c$ may
be chosen in the cone and outside that union. Fix such a $c$ and put
$\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon:=\mathrm{obj}+\varepsilon c$.

For $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, $\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon$ is non-constant on
every edge of $X(G)$: on an edge where $\mathrm{obj}$ is non-constant the sign
survives, and on an edge where it is constant the difference is
$\varepsilon\langle c,\cdot\rangle\ne0$. So $\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon$ is a
generic linear objective on a simple polytope combinatorially equivalent to the
$m$-cube, and the orientation $s''$ it induces is an LP orientation, hence an
AUSO satisfying Holt--Klee on every face (Holt--Klee; G\"artner--Morris--R\"ust),
exactly as in \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}.

Finally $s''(\sigma_t)=S_t$ for every $t$. If $(\sigma_t,v)$ is not tied the
edge is non-constant for $\mathrm{obj}$ and its sign, which is that of the
margin by the displayed identity, is preserved. If it is tied then
$(t,v)\in T$ and
$\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon(y^{\sigma_t[v]})-\mathrm{obj}_\varepsilon(y^{\sigma_t})
 =-\varepsilon\langle c,D_{t,v}\rangle<0$, so $v\notin s''(\sigma_t)$. Hence the
bottom-antipodal walk of $s''$ from $\sigma_0$ passes through
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_L$ and stops there, $s''(\sigma_L)=S_L=\emptyset$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{fs15:run-hk-cor}
If a one-player stopping SSG is nondegenerate at every strategy of its
all-switches run --- in particular, if it is nondegenerate --- then that run
has length at most $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$. Any one-player family whose
all-switches runs are superpolynomially long while
$h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}$ is polynomially bounded must therefore be degenerate
at at least \emph{two} incidences of each long run, and the corresponding
occupancy differences $D_{t,v}$ must positively span $0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Two ties never span]\label{fs15:two-ties}
Let $(t_1,v_1)$ and $(t_2,v_2)$ be tied incidences on the run of a one-player
stopping SSG with $v_1\ne v_2$ and $\sigma_{t_2}(v_1)\ne\sigma_{t_1}(v_1)$.
Then $0\notin\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t_1,v_1},D_{t_2,v_2}\}$. Consequently a
tie set $T$ with $|T|=2$ can fail the hypothesis of \Cref{fs15:run-hk} only if
either the two ties sit at the \emph{same} Max vertex with opposite actions
there, or they sit at different vertices $v_1\ne v_2$ and each of
$\sigma_{t_1},\sigma_{t_2}$ agrees with the other at both $v_1$ and $v_2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $a:=\sigma_{t_1}(v_1)$ and read the coordinate $(v_1,a)$ of
$\mathbb R^{2m}$. The vertex $y^{\sigma}$ is supported on
$\{(u,\sigma(u)):u\in\Vmax\}$ and is at least $\bbone$ there
(\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}). So $y^{\sigma_{t_1}}$ has mass
$\ge1$ at $(v_1,a)$ and $y^{\sigma_{t_1}[v_1]}$ has none, giving
$D_{t_1,v_1}[(v_1,a)]\ge1$; while $\sigma_{t_2}$ and $\sigma_{t_2}[v_2]$ both
take the action $1-a$ at $v_1$ --- they differ only at $v_2\ne v_1$ --- so
neither has mass at $(v_1,a)$ and $D_{t_2,v_2}[(v_1,a)]=0$. A convex
combination $c_1D_{t_1,v_1}+c_2D_{t_2,v_2}=0$ therefore forces $c_1=0$, hence
$c_2=1$ and $D_{t_2,v_2}=0$, which is false: the two vertices
$y^{\sigma_{t_2}}$ and $y^{\sigma_{t_2}[v_2]}$ have different supports. The
final sentence is the contrapositive, applied at $v_1$ and at $v_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What a two-tie escape must look like]\label{fs15:two-ties-cor}
Let $T=\{(t_1,v_1),(t_2,v_2)\}$ be the tied incidences on the run of a
one-player stopping SSG and suppose
$0\in\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t_1,v_1},D_{t_2,v_2}\}$. Then either
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $v_1=v_2=:v$ and $\sigma_{t_1}(v)\ne\sigma_{t_2}(v)$; or
\item $v_1\ne v_2$ and $\sigma_{t_1}$ agrees with $\sigma_{t_2}$ at both $v_1$
      and $v_2$.
\end{enumerate}
In case (i) the two strategies differ at some $u\notin\{v\}$, and for every
such $u$
\[
  y^{\sigma_{t_1}}_{u,\sigma_{t_1}(u)}=y^{\sigma_{t_1}[v]}_{u,\sigma_{t_1}(u)},
  \qquad
  y^{\sigma_{t_2}}_{u,\sigma_{t_2}(u)}=y^{\sigma_{t_2}[v]}_{u,\sigma_{t_2}(u)}:
\]
switching $v$ must leave the expected total occupancy of $u$ exactly unchanged,
although it changes the strategy there\,---\,at every coordinate on which the
two run strategies disagree.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{fs15:two-ties} gives the dichotomy, once one notes that $v_1=v_2=v$ with
$\sigma_{t_1}(v)=\sigma_{t_2}(v)=a$ is impossible: the coordinate $(v,a)$ then
receives $c_1y^{\sigma_{t_1}}_{v,a}+c_2y^{\sigma_{t_2}}_{v,a}$ with both terms
positive and both $y\ge1$, forcing $c_1=c_2=0$. In case (i), $\sigma_{t_2}$ is
neither $\sigma_{t_1}$ (distinct strategies of a run carry distinct value
vectors) nor $\sigma_{t_1}[v]$ (which is off the run, by
\Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c)), so they differ at some $u\ne v$. Fix such a $u$
and read the coordinate $(u,\sigma_{t_1}(u))$: since
$\sigma_{t_2}(u)\ne\sigma_{t_1}(u)$ and $\sigma_{t_2},\sigma_{t_2}[v]$ agree at
$u$, the vector $D_{t_2,v}$ vanishes there, so $c_1D_{t_1,v}[(u,\sigma_{t_1}(u))]=0$;
and $c_1\ne0$, since $c_1=0$ forces $D_{t_2,v}=0$. Hence
$D_{t_1,v}[(u,\sigma_{t_1}(u))]=0$, which is the first displayed equality; the
second is symmetric.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[$f_1(4)=6<f(4)=h^{\ast}(4)=7$]\label{fs15:f1-four}
No stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $|\Vmax|=4$ has an all-switches run
of length $7$, degenerate or not; and one with a run of length $6$ exists. So
$f_1(4)=6$, while $f(4)=h^{\ast}(4)=7$ is attained by the two-player game
$G^{\sharp}$ of \Cref{prop:auso-seven}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $L=7$. The AUSO $s'$ of \Cref{cor:ceiling-general} has a
bottom-antipodal walk of length $7$, so its height is at least $7=h^{\ast}(4)$,
hence exactly $7$; by \Cref{prop:auso-census} --- recomputed here from the
census of all $12640$ classes --- there is exactly one such class, of $384$
outmaps. Enumerating that orbit and, in each of its members, every start of
height $7$, gives $768$ pairs (outmap, walk). In each pair, the incidences
$(t,v)$ with $v\notin S_t$, $s'(\sigma_t\oplus2^v)=S_t\mathbin{|}2^v$ and
$\sigma_t\oplus2^v$ off the walk --- the only ones a tie can occupy, by
\Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c),(d) --- number at most one. So $|T|\le1$ and
\Cref{fs15:run-hk} supplies a Holt--Klee AUSO of the $4$-cube with a
bottom-antipodal walk of length $7$. But the greatest bottom-antipodal height
of a Holt--Klee AUSO of the $4$-cube is $6$: the census gives heights
$1,2,3,4,5,6$ for $1,423,2503,2401,729,56$ Holt--Klee classes and the single
height-$7$ class is not Holt--Klee. Contradiction.

For the lower bound, the one-player game
\texttt{AP\_m4\_k0\_den256\_s200} of \Cref{rem:blowup-measured} --- four Max
vertices, ninety-four average, denominator $256$ --- is stopping, every row of
its normal form leaking, is nondegenerate, and its all-switches run from
$\sigma=2$ is $2,8,5,9,13,14,15$, of length $6$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The second blow-up level needs Min vertices, ties allowed]\label{fs15:b2-oneplayer}
Let $W=\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_{10}$ be the bottom-antipodal walk of
$B^{2}$, the second level of \Cref{thm:blowup} seeded at the $1$-cube: on the
$5$-cube with the representative
\[
  B^{2}=(4,7,2,5,1,0,6,3,9,24,14,27,28,31,10,29,25,16,30,19,20,23,26,21,17,8,22,11,12,15,18,13),
\]
$W=13,18,12,16,9,17,1,6,0,4,5$ and
$S=31,30,28,25,24,16,7,6,4,1,0$. (The first level here is
$(1,0,6,3,4,7,2,5)$, the orientation of \Cref{rem:blowup-measured} translated
by $1$; the second level is a USO, acyclic, of height $10$, and not
Holt--Klee, as recorded there.) No stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ has
$W$ as an all-switches run --- degenerate or not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose one does, and let $s'$ be the AUSO of \Cref{cor:ceiling-general}, so
$s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ for $0\le t\le10$. An exhaustive depth-first enumeration of
the outmaps of the $5$-cube subject to those eleven values and to the
Szab\'o--Welzl condition (which already forces injectivity) returns $1897$
unique sink orientations, of which $875$ are acyclic --- $B^{2}$ among them ---
and \emph{none} is Holt--Klee. By \Cref{fs15:run-hk} the tie set $T$ therefore
satisfies $0\in\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t,v}\}$, so $|T|\ge2$.

By \Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c),(d), $T$ is contained in the set of $(t,v)$ with
$v\notin S_t$, $s'(\sigma_t\oplus2^v)=S_t\mathbin{|}2^v$ and
$\sigma_t\oplus2^v\notin W$. Over the $875$ orientations that set is
$\emptyset$ ($180$ times), $\{(7,3)\}$ ($297$), $\{(5,2)\}$ ($162$) or
$\{(5,2),(7,3)\}$ ($236$) --- never anything else. Hence
$T=\{(5,2),(7,3)\}$ and
$c_1D_{5,2}+c_2D_{7,3}=0$ with $c_1,c_2>0$.

Read that identity in the coordinate $(x_2,0)$ of $\mathbb R^{2m}$. Now
$\sigma_5=17$ has action $0$ at $x_2$, so
$D_{5,2}$ has entry $y^{\sigma_5}_{x_2,0}\ge1$ there, the second term
$y^{\sigma_5[x_2]}$ being supported on action $1$ at $x_2$; while $\sigma_7=6$
and $\sigma_7[x_3]=14$ both have action $1$ at $x_2$, so $D_{7,3}$ vanishes
there. The identity reads $c_1y^{\sigma_5}_{x_2,0}=0$, and
$y^{\sigma}\ge\bbone$ by \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}. Contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:b2-remark}
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured} says that the second level ``is not Holt--Klee, so
any realisation needs Min vertices''. Read through \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}
that argument covers nondegenerate realisations of the \emph{orientation};
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer} covers realisations of the \emph{walk}, which is all a
run needs, and covers degenerate ones. The two steps are independent of each
other: the first is that no Holt--Klee orientation agrees with the walk even at
its eleven vertices, which is stronger than $B^{2}$ itself failing Holt--Klee
and is what the walk-only relaxation would otherwise buy; the second is that
the two ties the combinatorics permits cannot both occur.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Walk realisation is a linear programme in the value vectors]\label{fs15:walk-lp}
Fix $m$, $k$, a walk $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ of Max strategies with
$S_t=\sigma_t\oplus\sigma_{t+1}$ and $S_L=\emptyset$, value vectors
$x_0,\dots,x_L\in\mathbb R^{n}$, $n=m+k$, and Min actions
$\tau_0,\dots,\tau_L\in\{0,1\}^{k}$. Consider the system, in the $2n$ rows
$(p^{w,a},q^{w,a})\ge0$ of a harmonic normal form:
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
  w\in\Vmax,\ \sigma_t(w)=a: & \langle p^{w,a},x_t\rangle+q^{w,a}=x_t(w),\\
  w\in\Vmax,\ \sigma_t(w)\ne a: & \langle p^{w,a},x_t\rangle+q^{w,a}\ \ge\ x_t(w)+\delta\ \ (w\in S_t),\quad
                                  \le x_t(w)\ \ (w\notin S_t),\\
  u\in\Vmin,\ \tau_t(u)=a: & \langle p^{u,a},x_t\rangle+q^{u,a}=x_t(u),\\
  u\in\Vmin,\ \tau_t(u)\ne a: & \langle p^{u,a},x_t\rangle+q^{u,a}\ \ge\ x_t(u),\\
  \multicolumn{2}{l}{|p^{w,a}|_1+q^{w,a}\le1-\varepsilon\quad\text{for every }(w,a).}
 \end{array}
\]
It is linear, and the constraints for distinct $(w,a)$ involve disjoint
unknowns, so it splits into $2n$ independent linear programmes in $n+1$
nonnegative unknowns and at most $L+2$ constraints. Any solution with
$\delta>0$ is a stopping game whose all-switches run from $\sigma_0$ is
exactly $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$ and whose value vectors along it are the
$x_t$; conversely every such game furnishes a solution, with $x_t:=\val_{\sigma_t}$
and $\tau_t$ a Min best response. Ties off the run are unconstrained, and ties
on it are exactly the inequalities met with equality.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Strict substochasticity makes each frozen operator a contraction, so
$\val_{\sigma_t}$ is its unique fixed point; the equalities together with the
Min inequalities say precisely that $x_t$ is that fixed point, and the Max
inequalities say precisely that $S(\sigma_t)=S_t$. The run visits only
$\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_L$, so no other strategy is constrained. Disjointness of
the unknowns is immediate: the row $(w,a)$ occurs in no condition indexed by a
different $(w',a')$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:walk-lp-remark}
\Cref{fs15:walk-lp} is the search this route used, and it inverts the
parametrisation of \Cref{prop:auso-seven}'s integer search and of
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured}'s: there the rows are the unknowns and the value
vectors are a rational function of them, so every condition is nonlinear; here
the value vectors are the unknowns and the rows are the output of $2n$ small
exact linear programmes. On $G^{\sharp}$ the reconstruction is immediate: from
its eight value vectors and Min responses alone the programme returns a
stopping game whose run from $\sigma=8$ is again $8,6,11,7,13,5,1,0$.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The separability hypothesis is not vacuous]\label{fs15:escape-real}
There is a one-player stopping SSG with four Max vertices whose all-switches
run carries two tied incidences at the \emph{same} Max vertex with opposite
actions, and whose two occupancy differences are exactly anti-parallel, so that
$0\in\operatorname{conv}\{D_{t,v}\}$ and the hypothesis of \Cref{fs15:run-hk}
fails. Its harmonic normal form has denominator $8$: with
$(p^{v,a};q^{v,a})$ listed over the targets $(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3;t_1)$,
\[
 \begin{array}{r@{\quad}l@{\qquad}l}
  x_0: & (0,\tfrac14,0,\tfrac18;\tfrac38) & (0,0,0,\tfrac18;0)\\
  x_1: & (\tfrac18,0,\tfrac14,\tfrac14;0) & (0,\tfrac12,\tfrac14,0;0)\\
  x_2: & (\tfrac14,0,\tfrac14,0;\tfrac18) & (0,\tfrac18,\tfrac18,0;0)\\
  x_3: & (0,\tfrac18,\tfrac18,\tfrac14;0) & (0,0,\tfrac14,0;0).
 \end{array}
\]
Every row leaks, so the game is stopping. Its all-switches run from
$\sigma_0=6$ is $6,0,10$; the incidences $(\sigma_0,x_3)$ and
$(\sigma_2,x_3)$ are tied, with $\sigma_0(x_3)=0$ and $\sigma_2(x_3)=1$; and
\[
  D_{0,x_3}=(0,0,0,\tfrac38,0,0,\tfrac32,-\tfrac98),\qquad
  D_{2,x_3}=-\tfrac{880}{819}\,D_{0,x_3}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
An exact rational computation from the displayed rows: the value vectors along
the run, the sixteen margins, the two occupancy vertices of each tied edge, and
the ratio. Independently, the Knuth--Yao construction of \Cref{lem:gadget}'s
kind turns those rows into an explicit stopping SSG on $31$ vertices --- four
Max, twenty-five average, two sinks --- whose greatest trap is empty and on
which the run, the value vectors and the two ties, recomputed from the game by
taking profile values, agree with the table.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:escape-remark}
So \Cref{fs15:run-hk} cannot be stated without its hypothesis, and
\Cref{fs15:two-ties} is sharp: the only two-tie configuration it leaves open is
the one \Cref{fs15:escape-real} exhibits. Whether that configuration can occur
on a run \emph{longer} than $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)$ --- which is what a
one-player superpolynomial family would need --- is the gap this route leaves.
The instance above has a run of length $2$, well under
$h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(4)=6$, and both of the walks of
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer,fs15:h12-oneplayer} rule the configuration out on
combinatorial grounds alone. Random search finds the configuration rarely: over
$15000$ one-player normal forms with $m=3$ and denominator $8$ ($120000$ runs,
$38782$ of them carrying a tie) it occurred once, and over $4000$ with $m=4$
and denominator $8$ ($64000$ runs, $24090$ with a tie) once.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[What the searches did and did not show]\label{fs15:search-remark}
\Cref{fs15:walk-lp} was also run as a search, over the value vectors and over
the game manifold with the programme as an inner optimal repair, on
$G^{\sharp}$'s own walk with two Min vertices and on the walk of
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer} with one and with two Min vertices. None converged:
after $3$--$5\times10^{4}$ evaluations each they plateau at a total hinge
violation near $6\times10^{-3}$. Since the calibration target ---
$G^{\sharp}$'s walk, which the programme reconstructs instantly from
$G^{\sharp}$'s own value vectors --- also fails, these runs are evidence about
the search and not about the instances, exactly as
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured} says of the earlier ones.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[The height-$12$ witness of \Cref{prop:hstar-five} needs Min vertices]\label{fs15:h12-oneplayer}
No stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ has
\[
  0,\,15,\,24,\,31,\,20,\,23,\,18,\,14,\,26,\,10,\,2,\,3,\,1
\]
--- the bottom-antipodal walk of length $12=h^{\ast}(5)$ of the outmap printed
in \Cref{prop:hstar-five} --- as its all-switches run.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The thirteen values $s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ determine the orientation completely:
the depth-first enumeration of \Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer}'s kind returns exactly
one outmap of the $5$-cube compatible with them, namely the printed one, and it
is not Holt--Klee. So \Cref{fs15:run-hk} makes the tie set $T$ non-separable,
whence $|T|\ge2$; and by \Cref{fs15:tie-partner}(c),(d) the only incidences a
tie can occupy are $(t,v)=(0,4)$ and $(7,1)$, with partners $16$ and $12$ off
the run. Hence $T=\{(0,4),(7,1)\}$. But $\sigma_7=14$ has action $1$ at the
Max vertex $x_1$ while $\sigma_0=0$ has action $0$ there, so
\Cref{fs15:two-ties} applies with $v_1=x_1$, $v_2=x_4$ and contradicts
non-separability.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[A decision procedure for one-player realisability of a walk]\label{fs15:screen}
The three impossibility results above are instances of one finite test, which
takes a walk $W$ of the $m$-cube and returns either ``no one-player stopping
SSG has $W$ as its all-switches run'' or ``undecided''. Enumerate every outmap
$s'$ of the $m$-cube with $s'(\sigma_t)=S_t$ along $W$ --- the Szab\'o--Welzl
condition forces injectivity and prunes hard, so this is a small search: $1$
completion for the walk of \Cref{fs15:h12-oneplayer}, $1897$ (of which $875$
acyclic) for that of \Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer}. Discard the cyclic ones. If some
survivor is Holt--Klee, return undecided. Otherwise compute, for each survivor,
the legal candidate tie set of \Cref{fs15:tie-partner}; if for every survivor
every candidate set is separable in the sense of \Cref{fs15:run-hk} --- for
which \Cref{fs15:two-ties} is usually enough --- return the impossibility. The
cost is dominated by the completion enumeration and is independent of any
search over games. Applied to the $768$ length-$7$ walks of the $4$-cube it
gives $f_1(4)=6$; applied to the two $5$-cube walks above it gives
\Cref{fs15:b2-oneplayer,fs15:h12-oneplayer}. What it does not give is a bound
on $f_1(5)$: that would need the test on every length-$12$ walk of the
$5$-cube, of which \Cref{prop:hstar-five}'s enumeration counts $347640$ from
$\sigma_0=0$, about $2900$ up to the coordinate permutations that fix
$\sigma_0$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The top average vertex}\label{sec:fs15-top}

\Cref{lem:alphabet-cover} already contains the structure that the question
about the largest average value needs, and two consequences of it are worth
recording before the question is answered.

\begin{corollary}[The second letter is at least a half]\label{fs15:nu-half}
Let $G$ be stopping with $\Vavg\ne\emptyset$ and let
$\nu:=\max_{c\in\Vavg}\val(c)$. Then every value of $G$ is $1$ or at most
$\nu$, and $\nu\in\{0\}\cup[\tfrac12,1]$. Dually the least positive letter is
at most $\tfrac12$, and more generally the letters
$1=\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\dots$ satisfy $\lambda_i\ge2^{1-i}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every letter $\lambda\in(0,1)$ is attained at an average vertex by
\Cref{lem:alphabet-cover}, so no value lies strictly between $\nu$ and $1$, and
$\nu$ is the second letter. If $0<\nu<1$ then \Cref{lem:alphabet-cover} writes
$\nu=\tfrac12(\lambda_i+\lambda_j)$ with $\lambda_i<\nu<\lambda_j$; the only
letter above $\nu$ is $1$, so $\nu=\tfrac12(1+\lambda_i)\ge\tfrac12$. The same
lemma gives $\lambda_i\ge\tfrac12\lambda_{i-1}$ for every interior $i$, whence
$\lambda_i\ge2^{1-i}$; the dual statements are \Cref{lem:duality}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:half-free}
So $\max_{v}\val(v)\ge\tfrac12$ unless every value is $0$ or $1$, and which of
the two holds is decided in linear time by the attractor sweeps that compute
$\{\val=0\}$ and $\{\val=1\}$. The question ``does some vertex have value at
least $\tfrac12$?'' is therefore free, while ``does \emph{this} vertex have
value at least $\tfrac12$?'' is \Cref{prob:main}. The threshold $\tfrac12$
plays no part in the difficulty; the naming of a vertex does.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[$\textsc{Top}$ is the whole problem]\label{fs15:top}
Let $\textsc{Top}$ be the problem: given a stopping SSG with
$\Vavg\ne\emptyset$, output an average vertex of maximum value. Then
$\textsc{Top}$ is polynomial-time equivalent to \Cref{prob:main}, by a
reduction making a single oracle call.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
One direction is trivial. For the other, by \Cref{prop:no-halving}(b) it is
enough to reduce the comparison of two vertices $p,q$ of a stopping $G$ to
$\textsc{Top}$. Compute $\{\val=1\}$ and $\{\val=0\}$ by the attractor sweeps
and redirect every edge into them to $t_1$ and $t_0$ respectively; values are
unchanged, the game stays stopping, and afterwards every non-sink value lies in
$(0,1)$. If $p$ or $q$ has been absorbed into a sink the comparison is already
decided; otherwise let $a:=|\Vavg|$ of the reduced game --- if $a=0$ every
value is $0$ or $1$ and there is nothing to decide --- and put $r:=2a+2$,
$m:=r+2$.

Adjoin a reference chain $e_1\to(t_1,t_0)$, $e_{j+1}\to(t_1,e_j)$ of $r$
average vertices, so $\val(e_j)=1-2^{-j}$; and two boost chains
\[
  c^{(1)}_p\to(t_1,p),\quad c^{(j+1)}_p\to(t_1,c^{(j)}_p),
  \qquad
  c^{(1)}_q\to(e_r,q),\quad c^{(j+1)}_q\to(t_1,c^{(j)}_q),
\]
of $m$ average vertices each. Nothing new is a successor of anything old, so
the old values are unchanged and the game is still stopping. By induction
\[
  \val(c^{(m)}_p)=1-\frac{1-\val(p)}{2^{m}},\qquad
  \val(c^{(m)}_q)=1-\frac{1-\val(q)+2^{-r}}{2^{m}} .
\]
Both are at least $1-2^{-(m-1)}=1-2^{-(r+1)}$, which strictly exceeds every
$\val(e_j)\le1-2^{-r}$ and every old average value: an old value is $<1$ with
denominator dividing an integer at most $2^{a}$ (\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}),
hence at most $1-2^{-a}$, and $r+1>a$. Within each boost chain the values
increase with $j$, so the maximum over $\Vavg$ is attained at $c^{(m)}_p$ or at
$c^{(m)}_q$ (an intermediate of one chain may well exceed the top of the other,
which does not matter), and
\[
  \val(c^{(m)}_p)>\val(c^{(m)}_q)
  \iff \val(p)>\val(q)-2^{-r}.
\]
Two distinct old values differ by at least $2^{-2a}>2^{-r}$, again by
\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}, and $\val(q)-\val(p)=2^{-r}$ is impossible for
the same reason; so the right-hand side holds exactly when
$\val(p)\ge\val(q)$, the maximiser is unique, and the single oracle answer
decides the comparison. The construction adds $r+2m=O(a)$ vertices.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fs15:top-remark}
So the answer to the question raised for \Cref{thm:order-determines} is that
naming the top average vertex buys the whole game and costs the whole game:
\textsc{Top} joins \Cref{thm:compare-equivalence,thm:decide-one-bit,%
prop:no-halving,cor:wrong-equivalence,rem:alphabet-equivalence} on the list of
target-equivalent reformulations. The peeling recursion it suggests --- know
the top letter, remove it, recurse --- is blocked at the first step for the
reason \Cref{prop:no-halving}(a) gives: removing a letter means substituting a
known value, and that costs $a$ fresh average vertices.
\end{remark}
